questions.question: Why does the lesson evaluate the assembled pipeline against the same qrels used for its component comparisons?
options: A component test cannot be written in Python
The qrels are needed only to calculate latency
Only the end-to-end run shows whether chunking, retrieval, reranking, generation, and scoring compose without an interface failure
The generator is the only stage that changes between pipelines
questions.explanation: The shared qrels make the baseline, hybrid, and hybrid-plus-rerank outputs comparable. Running the complete path then reveals integration regressions that isolated metrics can miss.

questions.question: What is the role of refuse-on-low-confidence in the answer generator?
options: It logs every refusal to disk
It blocks queries longer than 100 tokens
It triggers a re-retrieval with a different chunker
It returns 'I do not know' when the reranker top-1 score sits below a corpus-specific threshold, preventing hallucinated answers when the retrieved context does not address the query
questions.explanation: A consistently low rank-1 score is the model telling you nothing in the corpus answers this query; refuse rather than hallucinate.

questions.question: Why are the rerank training triples kept disjoint from the eval queries?
options: To prevent train-test leakage; if the eval queries overlap the rerank training set the eval looks magical and the regression test does not catch real drift
To save GPU memory
Because the cross-encoder requires distinct vocabularies
Because RRF cannot fuse overlapping lists
questions.explanation: Strict separation is the basic hygiene; otherwise the rerank metric does not predict production behavior.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the self-terminating demo's exit code?
options: Cosmetic
It encodes pass/fail against the metric thresholds; a CI smoke test can plug the demo into the pipeline and gate the merge on a non-zero exit
It is required by Python
The reranker uses it as a training signal
questions.explanation: Exit code 0 means thresholds met; non-zero means regression. That is the contract a CI gate consumes.

questions.question: What does a citation anchor look like in this pipeline?
options: Markdown link with the source URL
JSON-RPC envelope
[doc_id:chunk_index]
The literal embedding vector
questions.explanation: The generator emits the (doc_id, chunk_index) tuple as an anchor so a downstream UI or auditor can map every claim back to its source chunk.

questions.question: Which failure mode is invisible to the mock generator and must be tested with a real LLM before shipping?
options: Latency
Tokenization
Vector index size
Hallucination: the mock generator only emits text from retrieved chunks and cannot invent content; a real LLM can ignore the chunks and generate ungrounded answers
questions.explanation: The mock cannot test the generator's safety against hallucinated content; only a real model swap-in can.
